title: Exp-concave dynamic online optimization: unknown Euclidean path budget and full information.
summary: One learner must adapt to all comparator paths without knowing path length in advance. Losses are exponentially concave, path length is Euclidean, and the complete current function is revealed after acting.

model.instance: The learner acts in the same nonempty compact convex set $W\subset\mathbb R^d$ each round and is compared simultaneously with every comparator path $u_{1:T}\in W^T$. Losses are differentiable and exp-concave on $W$: $$\operatorname{diam}_2(W)\le D,\qquad e^{-\eta f_t(\cdot)}\ \text{on }W\text{ is concave},\qquad \|\nabla f_t(w)\|_2\le G\quad(\forall t,\ w\in W).$$ The upper bound holds for each admissible realized loss sequence; the recorded lower bound uses a sequence fixed before interaction. For dimension optimality, $D,G,\eta$ are fixed independently of $d,T$. Precisely, exp-concavity means that for each round $t$, the map $x\mapsto\exp(-\eta f_t(x))$ is concave on the stated feasible set. It concerns the full action variable, with the norm and gradient bounds specified here.

$$

operations.query_signature: Submit $w_t\in W$, incur $f_t(w_t)$, and then receive the full function $f_t$. Its values and gradients may subsequently be evaluated at other points, without observation noise. The public projection interface provides exact Mahalanobis projections for any positive definite metric $A\succ0$; each such projection has arithmetic cost $C_{\mathrm{proj}}(d)$. $$\Pi_W^A(z)\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{w\in W}(w-z)^{\mathsf T}A(w-z).$$ Inputs $d,T,D,G,\eta$, the set $W$, and its projection interface are public. Neither the comparator path $u_{1:T}$ nor its total path length $P_T^{(2)}$ is supplied. Past feedback may be stored and reused computationally; no unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available beyond the explicitly declared within-round interface.

components.description: $T$ sequential rounds, or $T$ rounds per task

$T$ is the online horizon. The algorithm covering the full stated range uses $O(\log T)$ loss evaluations, gradient evaluations, and Euclidean projections per round, including the internal work of the exp-concave branch. The following expressions give total dense spectral/projection arithmetic and storage, respectively; storage counts real numbers, not bits: $$\text{arithmetic cost}=O\!\left(T\bigl(d^3+C_{\mathrm{proj}}(d)\bigr)\log^2(2T)\right),\qquad \text{storage}=O\!\left(d^2\log^2(2T)\right).$$ This specification provides full-function feedback. The single-gradient-at-the-action variant is a separate information contract, so these resources cannot be described as one gradient call per round. Exploration, initialization, and identification count toward the online budget. Oracle calls, arithmetic, communication rounds/bits, and memory remain separate resources; no optimal arithmetic or bit complexity is asserted.

guarantees.complete_expression: The upper bound is deterministic and holds pathwise: the same algorithm works simultaneously for every admissible loss sequence and comparator path. The lower bound considers the expression below, with expectation only over learner randomness. The quantity $P$ is an analytical comparator budget, not a known algorithm input. $$\inf_{\mathcal A}\ \sup_{\substack{f_{1:T}\ \text{admissible},\ u_{1:T}\in W^T\\ P_T^{(2)}(u)\le P}}\ \mathbb E_{\mathcal A}\!\left[\operatorname{Reg}_T(u)\right].$$
